extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents and applicants) preparing or prosecuting U.S. plant patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and examination standards for preparing, filing, and examining U.S. plant patent applications under the Plant Patent Act (35 U.S.C. 161-164) and related USPTO rules. Covers eligibility, specification content, drawings, specimens, examination, ARS reports, UPOV denomination issues, and issuance requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant patent statutory eligibility (35 U.S.C. 161)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whoever invents or discovers and asexually reproduces any distinct and new variety of plant, including cultivated sports, mutants, hybrids, and newly found seedlings, other than a tuber propagated plant or a plant found in an uncultivated state, may obtain a patent therefor, subject to the conditions and requirements of this title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plant patents apply to asexually reproduced distinct and new varieties; exclude tuber-propagated plants (in narrow horticultural sense) and plants found in an uncultivated state. The Plant Patent Act provisions apply except as otherwise provided in the patent laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and examples of asexually propagated plants
rubrics_metrics.description: Asexually propagated plants are those reproduced by means other than from seeds, such as by the rooting of cuttings, by layering, budding, grafting, inarching, apomictic seeds, bulbs, division, slips, rhizomes, runners, corms, tissue culture, nucellar embryos, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plants capable of sexual reproduction are not excluded if they have also been asexually reproduced. Examples include cultivated sports, mutants, hybrids, and transformed plants; algae and macro-fungi are regarded as plants for this purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tuber-propagated plant exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Plant patents cannot be obtained for tuber propagated plants; the term 'tuber' is used in its narrow horticultural sense meaning a short, thickened portion of an underground branch (e.g., Irish potato, Jerusalem artichoke).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This exception exists because these plants are propagated by the same part sold as food. Check whether the plant falls within that narrow horticultural meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordinary meaning of 'plant' (scope and exclusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Plant' is interpreted in the ordinary and accepted sense, not the strict scientific sense, and thus excludes bacteria; a plant in ordinary meaning includes a living plant organism expressing a set of characteristics determined by its genotype and duplicable by asexual reproduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat asexual propagating material per se as the plant; consider whether the organism expresses a genotype duplicable by asexual reproduction (case law examples cited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-step invention requirement: discovery and asexual reproduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Invention for a plant patent is a two-step process: (1) discovery (identifying a novel plant, off-type, desirable mutant, or outstanding progeny); and (2) asexual reproduction and observation of propagules/clones to confirm identity and stability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both steps must be satisfied before filing. Filing before completing asexual reproduction/testing will result in rejection as premature and nonstatutory. The asexual reproduction step requires sufficient observation time to assure characteristics are not due to transient disease or environmental effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stability and uniformity testing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Asexual reproduction includes observation of resulting propagules or clones for a sufficient amount of time to conclude that such specimens are identical to the parent plant in all characteristics, testing stability and uniformity so that unique characteristics are not due to transient factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners and applicants must ensure the specification and supporting evidence show the plant is genetically stable and not the result of temporary conditions; insufficient testing supports rejection as premature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative protection under utility patents (35 U.S.C. 101)
rubrics_metrics.description: An asexually reproduced plant may alternatively be protected under 35 U.S.C. 101 (utility patent) provided the written description requirement can be satisfied; an application under 101 may claim the same asexually reproduced plant as under 161 and may include plant materials and processes involving plant materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider double patenting and obviousness-type double patenting rejections across 101 and 161 filings; filing a terminal disclaimer may be appropriate in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of grant for plant patents (35 U.S.C. 163)
rubrics_metrics.description: The grant shall include the right to exclude others from asexually reproducing the plant, and from using, offering for sale, or selling the plant so reproduced, or any of its parts, throughout the United States, or from importing the plant so reproduced, or any parts thereof, into the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rights are analogous to utility patents but focused on asexually reproduced plants and their parts; recognize that issued plant patents are regarded as limited to one plant/genome—derived sports/mutants may not be covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant patent term
rubrics_metrics.description: A plant patent issuing from an application filed after June 7, 1995 has a term which expires 20 years after the filing date of the application, or any earlier filing date claimed under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121 or 365(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculate term from the effective filing date as with other patents; be mindful of priority claims that may affect term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of general patent rules (37 CFR 1.161)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules relating to applications for patent for other inventions or discoveries are also applicable to applications for patents for plants except as otherwise provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use MPEP guidance for general procedural matters unless plant-specific rules provide exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements and order of a plant application (37 CFR 1.163(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicable, the plant application elements should appear in the following order: (1) Plant application transmittal form; (2) Fee transmittal form; (3) Application data sheet (§1.76); (4) Specification; (5) Drawings (in duplicate); (6) Inventor's oath or declaration (§1.162).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specified order and include required elements to avoid formal objections or requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor and oath/declaration requirements for plant applications (37 CFR 1.162)
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor named must be the person who has invented or discovered and asexually reproduced the new and distinct variety; the oath/declaration must state that the inventor has asexually reproduced the plant and if newly found, that it was found in a cultivated area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joint inventorship is possible (e.g., one discovered/selects, another reproduced and verified); those merely performing propagation services are not inventors. Use form PTO/AIA/09 for post-AIA plant application declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification disclosure standard for plant patents (35 U.S.C. 162; 37 CFR 1.163(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must contain as full and complete a disclosure as possible of the plant and the characteristics thereof that distinguish the same over related known varieties, and its antecedents, and must particularly point out where and in what manner the variety of plant has been asexually reproduced. For a newly found plant, the specification must particularly point out the location and character of the area where the plant was discovered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 35 U.S.C. 162 relaxes section 112 for plant patents ('as complete as is reasonably possible'), but the specification still must be botanically complete. Use botanical terms and include origin/parentage; failure to particularly point out asexual reproduction or discovery location supports objection under form paragraphs (e.g., ¶16.01, ¶16.10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Single claim and form of claim (37 CFR 1.164)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim shall be in formal terms to the new and distinct variety of the specified plant as described and illustrated, and may also recite the principal distinguishing characteristics. More than one claim is not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only one claim is necessary and permitted; method claims are improper in a plant patent. Example proper claim: 'A new and distinct variety of hybrid tea rose plant, substantially as illustrated and described herein.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Required sections of the specification (37 CFR 1.163(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification should include, in order if applicable: (1) Title; (2) Cross-reference to related applications; (3) Statement regarding federally sponsored research; (4) Latin name of genus and species; (5) Variety denomination; (6) Background; (7) Brief summary; (8) Brief description of drawing; (9) Detailed botanical description; (10) A single claim; (11) Abstract of the disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text sections should be preceded by upper-case headings. Latin name and variety denomination should be clearly stated (see form paragraph ¶16.05 for missing denomination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Botanical-style detailed description requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification should include a complete detailed description of the plant and the characteristics which distinguish it over related known varieties, expressed in botanical terms in the general form followed in standard botanical textbooks or publications dealing with the varieties of the kind of plant involved, rather than broad nonbotanical characterizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include origin/parentage and genus/species; avoid nursery-catalog style broad descriptions. Use recognized botanical conventions to describe distinguishing characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Particularity re: manner and location of asexual reproduction (37 CFR 1.163(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must particularly point out where and in what manner the variety of plant has been asexually reproduced; for newly found plants, the specification must particularly point out the location and character of the area where the plant was discovered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to disclose these matters leads to objections (¶16.01 Specification, Manner of Asexually Reproducing; ¶16.10 Specification, Location of Plant Not Disclosed). Provide sufficient factual detail to meet the requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color disclosure and evidence requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where color is a distinctive feature of the plant, the color should be positively identified in the specification by reference to a designated color as given by a recognized color dictionary or color chart; color drawings/photographs may be required and must be submitted in duplicate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ¶16.02 and ¶16.03 where colors fail to correspond with those shown or color disclosure is unsupported. Two color copies are required; failure to include duplicates leads to correction requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance for corrected or substituted descriptions (limited)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the written description of a plant is deficient in certain respects, a clarification or additional description, or even a wholesale substitution of the original description so long as not totally inconsistent and unrelated to the original description and photograph, may be submitted in reply to an Office action and will not constitute new matter under 35 U.S.C. 132.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this limited opportunity to correct deficiencies, citing case law (e.g., Jessel v. Newland). Ensure amendments are consistent with original disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit of biological materials not required for plant patents
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules on Deposit of Biological Materials, 37 CFR 1.801-1.809, do not apply to plant patent applications in view of the reduced disclosure requirements of 35 U.S.C. 162, even where a deposit has been made in conjunction with a utility application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on deposit rules for meeting plant patent disclosure; instead provide botanical description and necessary specimens only when requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing standards and requirements (37 CFR 1.165; 1.84)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plant patent drawings should be artistically and competently executed and must disclose all the distinctive characteristics of the plant capable of visual representation. Drawings may be in color and must be in duplicate if color is distinguishing. Drawings must satisfy paper, size, margin, numbering, view arrangement, scale, and other standards specified in 37 CFR 1.84.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical details include acceptable sheet sizes (A4 or 8.5x11), margin sizes, no frames around sight, scan target points, sheet numbering conventions, view numbering ('FIG.' rules), no holes in drawing sheets, and that inadequate scale or poor execution are grounds for objection (¶16.06, ¶16.07, ¶16.11). If color is distinguishing, two color copies are required and failure to provide duplicates leads to correction before examination proceeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specimens: when required and submission guidance (37 CFR 1.166)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may be required to furnish specimens of the plant, or its flower or fruit, in a quantity and at a time in its stage of growth as may be designated, for study and inspection; such specimens must be properly packed and forwarded according to instructions. When it is not possible to forward specimens, plants must be made available for official inspection where grown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should not submit specimens unless specifically called for by the examiner. Use Form Paragraph ¶16.13 to require specimens when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination standards applicable to plant patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Plant applications are subject to the same examination process as other national applications with respect to patentable subject matter, utility, novelty, obviousness, disclosure, and claim specificity (35 U.S.C. 101, 102, 103, and 112). The sole exception in applicability of these statutory provisions is set forth in 35 U.S.C. 162.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior art searches should include appropriate patent subclasses and patent/non-patent literature databases. Consider ARS or USDA input where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and treatment of Agricultural Research Service (ARS) reports (35 U.S.C. 164; 37 CFR 1.167)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Office may submit applications to the Department of Agriculture for study and report (ARS). The report may embody criticisms, objections, suggestions for correction, or a statement that the variety described is not identical with others known to ARS specialists. The ARS report is advisory and placed in the file but not given a paper number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners may include portions of ARS reports in Office actions. Matters in the ARS report within the personal knowledge of ARS specialists are not sufficient basis for rejection unless supported by affidavits (37 CFR 1.104(d)(2)). Use Form ¶16.12 to reference ARS reports; do not treat ARS reports as automatic conclusive evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim and title must be directed to the entire plant (not flower/fruit alone)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim language must be such that it is directed to the 'new and distinct variety of plant.' Under no circumstance should the claim be directed to a new variety of flower or fruit in contradistinction to the plant bearing the flower or the tree bearing the fruit. The title of the invention must relate to the entire plant and not to its flower or fruit (e.g., 'Apple Tree', 'Rose Plant').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners may amend to insert words like 'tree' if necessary. Avoid claims/titles suggesting only fruit or flower are claimed. The specification should avoid unwarranted advertising or laudatory expressions and unnecessary statements about products made from fruit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on advertising and laudatory language in specification
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification should not contain unwarranted advertising (e.g., 'the disclosed plant being grown in the XYZ Nurseries of Topeka, Kansas') or laudatory expressions (e.g., 'The rose is prettier than any other rose').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such statements are irrelevant and should be deleted; examiners should object and require removal when present.

rubrics_metrics.name: UPOV Convention and variety denomination registration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: As a condition for receiving a plant patent it is necessary to register a variety denomination for that plant. Inclusion of the variety denomination in the plant patent application comprises its registration. The examiner must evaluate the proposed denomination in light of UPOV Convention Article 13 to ensure it is not identical with or confusingly similar to other names for the same or closely related species and is not misleading to the average consumer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordinarily the denomination proposed for registration in the United States must be the same as the denomination registered in another UPOV member state. The Latin name and variety denomination may be included in the application data sheet (ADS) per 37 CFR 1.76(b)(3). Use Form ¶16.05 (and ¶16.05.01) to object when denomination or Latin name is missing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of priority based on plant breeder's rights application (35 U.S.C. 119(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 119(f), an application for a plant patent may rely upon an application for plant breeder’s rights filed in a WTO member country (or in a foreign UPOV Contracting Party) for priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(a) through (c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use priority provisions when appropriate; be aware that UPOV/Paris Convention interactions may vary depending on national breeder's rights regimes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue requirements and printing choices for plant patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparation of a plant patent application for issue involves the same procedure as for other applications, with the exception that where there are color drawings, the better of the two color copies is selected for printing in the patent. International Patent Classification symbols should be placed on the Issue Classification form. All plant applications should contain an abstract when allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure abstracts present the plant concisely; when color drawings exist, select the best copy for printing; include IPC symbols for classification.
